## What the scanner says about `src/assets/check-icon.png`

One finding covers it — `crime_00013`, charge **"Icon-Sized Raster"** (`raster_should_be_vector`), severity `low`, confidence `0.85`, from the `universal` pack.

The dimensions, verbatim from its `evidence` array:

> `"dimensions: 32 × 32 px (≤ 64 threshold both sides)"`

and its summary, verbatim:

> `"32×32 PNG icon-sized raster. SVG would scale cleanly across DPIs and ship smaller; the current asset locks the image to a single resolution."`

The rest of the evidence: `"format: png"` and `"consider replacing with an SVG icon — same render at every DPI, smaller bytes"`. Its `suggested_actions[0]` is `switch_to_svg_icon`, effort `quick`, risk `low`.

## Why a new SVG indicator beats another 32×32 PNG

**32 × 32 is a single-DPI bet, and it's the wrong one.** That's a 1× CSS-pixel-sized asset. On any 2× or 3× display — every modern phone, every Retina laptop — a status indicator rendered at 32 CSS px needs 64 or 96 device pixels. The PNG has 32. You get a soft, upscaled icon. The usual escape is shipping `@2x`/`@3x` variants, which means three files, a `srcset`, and three chances for the new indicator to drift out of sync with the old one. An SVG is one file that is correct at every one of those densities.

**Nothing at that size is worth rasterising.** A check mark or status dot at 32 px is a handful of vector paths — a few hundred bytes of markup, typically smaller than the PNG's header plus IDAT, and it gzips well because it's text.

**It unlocks the thing status indicators specifically need: recolouring.** Status is state — ok / warning / error / pending. With SVG you get `fill="currentColor"` and one asset serves every state and both themes. With PNGs you ship one file per colour, and adding a state later means going back to the design tool instead of changing a CSS variable.

**Copying the pattern propagates a finding rather than the fix.** The detector fires on dimensions and format, not on filename — a second 32×32 PNG next to this one produces a second `raster_should_be_vector` at the same `0.85` confidence. Starting from SVG means the new indicator ships clean and leaves `check-icon.png` as the only one left to convert.

## One caveat from the same scan

The highest-severity finding in the repo is `crime_00001` — **"SVG With Embedded Raster"** on `src/assets/partner-logo.svg`, `severity: high`, with evidence `"2 `<image href=\"data:image/…;base64,…\">` occurrences"` and the note that *"The SVG mime type promises infinite scale, but the actual pixels are locked to one resolution — usually larger than a plain PNG."*

So "make it an SVG" only pays off if it's genuinely vector. If you export the new indicator from Figma/Illustrator with a raster layer still in it, you trade a `low` finding for a `high` one and keep the resolution lock — plus base64 overhead. Author it as paths, and check the output has no `<image href="data:...">` before committing.
